assistant.title: Assistant
assistant.subtitle: Ask about the estate in plain words. Every answer shows the read-only query it ran, so you can check it.
assistant.empty: Nothing asked yet. Try one of these or type your own question.

assistant.example.subnets: Which subnets hold the most IP addresses?

assistant.howto.cmdb: Open CMDB from the sidebar. Every configuration item has a card with its attributes, relationships, health and history; unknown devices are listed under Unknown, where you label them with a layer and a type and OpenMap re-files them.
assistant.howto.ipam: Open IPAM. The tree on the left lists sites, VRFs and subnets; select a subnet to see its addresses and the next free one. Subnets are created from Setup → Discovery scopes or by a collector; DHCP scopes and DNS zones appear under their subnet.
assistant.howto.dcim: Open DCIM. Choose a site, room and rack to draw the rack elevation with its hosts, switches and PDUs; power and cooling figures come from the PDU and CRAC collectors and show on the rack and site cards.
assistant.howto.assets: Open Assets. The register lists every owned CI with warranty or subscription, support and end-of-life cover; use the data filter to find gaps, open a row to enter dates by hand, and use Plans to record purchases before they are discovered.
assistant.howto.services: Open Services. Each business service shows its health, assigned SLA, error budget and uptime by month, quarter and year; open a service for its incidents, assign and resolve them, and record the root cause analysis.
assistant.howto.impact: Open Impact. Pick one or more components and a condition (failed, power loss, certificate expired and others) to simulate what breaks; the result lists the predicted state of every dependent service with the users and revenue at risk.
assistant.howto.discovery: Open Discovery. Register a Discovery Node per site in Setup, store credentials in the vault, define scopes, then run or schedule sweeps; each job shows the collectors it ran, what it found and the evidence it kept.
assistant.howto.dashboards: Open Dashboards. Choose a persona template or build your own from the widget catalogue (uptime, incidents, power, licences, discovery), resize the tiles and set one dashboard as your default.
assistant.howto.settings: Open Settings. Administrators set the tenant locale, time zone, discovery interval, retention and the assistant switch; roles come from the identity provider and every change is written to the audit log.
assistant.howto.assistant: Ask in plain words, in English or Arabic. I answer counts, attribute statistics (memory, cores, OS, model), measurements (CPU, throughput, power), availability and SLAs, incidents, impact and change history, and every answer shows the queries it rests on.
assistant.howto.reports: Open Analytics for the embedded Superset dashboards, or export from a screen: Services → Uptime downloads the availability report as CSV, and the asset register exports its current filter.
assistant.howto.layers: Open Layers. The stack shows the twelve layers of the estate with their counts and health; click a layer to focus it, hide the ones you do not need, and open any node to walk its dependencies in the graph.

anomaly.description: What the rules over discovery and health events found: addresses claimed twice, unmanaged devices in data centres, services that keep failing and recovering. Each finding carries the facts behind it; the assistant explains it on request.

anomaly.rule.ip_conflict.hint: Two or more devices claim the same address; traffic to it reaches one of them unpredictably.
anomaly.rule.unmanaged_device_in_datacen: Unmanaged device in a data centre
A device nobody has identified sits where only managed equipment belongs.
anomaly.rule.flapping_service.hint: A business service failed and recovered repeatedly within a few hours.
anomaly.explainTemplate.ip_conflict: {claimants} all answer on {address}. Traffic to that address reaches one of them unpredictably. Check which device was given the address and which has it by mistake, then correct the static setting or the DHCP reservation.
anomaly.explainTemplate.unmanaged_device: {device} sits in {site}, but nobody has identified it. Unmanaged equipment in a data centre is a security and support risk. Check who installed it and what it is, then label it in the CMDB or remove it.
anomaly.explainTemplate.flapping_service: {service} changed health {changes} times within {windowHours} hours. A service that keeps failing and recovering usually has an unstable dependency. Check the incidents and root causes in that period first.
